detail.longDescription:
I’m currently running a bunch of services behind a reverse proxy and that proxy
is configured to use let’s encrypt for ssl certs using DNS-01 challenges for
renewals. All of the services are configured to only work using Tailscale IPs,
so, as far as I’m aware, none of the services are open to the internet, except
for port 80. I noticed if I don’t leave port 80 open, when it’s time for
renewal, everything fails. This leads to a bunch of logs on my Unifi setup
saying intrusion attempts have been blocked on port 80. I thought I could go to
Let’s Encrypt’s website and find a list of IPs I could put on an allow list but
they don’t post those. So my questions are: 1. If I understand the process
correctly, Let’s Encrypt checks the DNS TXT record to verify I own a domain,
then sends a new cert to my server over port 80; meaning, I have to have port 80
open during the renewal process, correct? Nope 2. If that’s correct, what do you
all do about port 80? Do you just have a script to open the port during the
renewal process and close it afterwards or do you just leave it open all the
time? Is there maybe a tool that already has this functionality? not if using
DNS-01 challenges 3. I think I have port 443 open as well but I don’t remember
if that’s needed or if I just did that when I opened port 80 trying to get all
my services working again. Does 443 need to be open too? not if using DNS-01
challenges 4. If there is a better way to do all this or if I fucked up
somewhere, please share. This was just the first setup I got working. I fucked
up, see below Thanks EDIT: After deleting the current certificate and going
through the process of generating a new one, everything is working without port
80 open. I’m using NGINX Proxy Manager and I must have clicked on “Lets Encrypt
via HTTP” and not “Lets Encrypt via DNS” when originally setting this up. Not
sure how else this could have happened 😅
